decisions.reason: The source removes only the print version and states that the remaining scope is unchanged, so the digital flipbook deliverable remains active as specified.
Two-page spread behavior and even page-count requirements apply to the digital flipbook and are unaffected by removal of the print version.
The platform workflow is specific to the retained digital flipbook; removing the separate print output does not change its platform requirements.
The magazine still requires layout, typesetting, formatting, and assembly for the digital deliverable, and the source explicitly leaves the remaining scope unchanged.
Template creation remains necessary for the magazine layout independently of whether a print-ready version is delivered.
The digital magazine still needs an accurate table of contents based on finalized pagination; the print-output removal does not alter that requirement.
Image-quality enhancement remains part of the retained publication scope and is not limited to the removed print-ready output.
Advertisement clarity remains required in the digital publication; historical references to trim and bleed do not make the current clarity requirement dependent on the print deliverable.
Accurate cover page references remain necessary for the retained digital magazine and are unaffected by removal of the print version.
The issue month and edition label describe publication metadata and do not depend on delivery of a print-ready version.
The tribute page remains required content in the magazine regardless of whether the separate print version is delivered.
Author names, photographs, and placement remain article-presentation requirements for the retained digital magazine and are unaffected by the print-version removal.
